Meet the two artists who turn the moon's light into music.
We're going to turn now to some far-out music.
(SOUNDBITE OF KYLE SIMON AND BRIAN WEITZ'S "THE SIRENS PT. 1")
And what exactly do you mean by that, Scott?
DETROW: That is a great question. As you know, space does not have sound. So this is not actually music of the moon.
DETROW: What we hear right now is the creation of artist Kyle Simon and musician Brian Weitz.
BRIAN WEITZ: I am taking the voltage from the moonlight and feeding it into my synthesizer.
DETROW: So to get that voltage, Simon created a way to capture the moonlight.

KYLE SIMON: First, I built a telescope, and we equipped it with these different diodes. Light comes in and a voltage goes out. The brightest lights or, you know, certain frequencies of light produce different voltages.
SUMMERS: So this music is from the full moon in October 2024. The pair recorded those sounds and turned them into an album. It's called "The Sirens."

SIMON: I'm really into mythology, and so the idea of the sirens in The Odyssey is something that's always intrigued me, you know? Like, when I first started building telescopes and spending all my nights outside, looking at the stars, they fill your head with all these questions and philosophical ideas, and you're just like, agh (ph), you know? Like, start going crazy from it.
SUMMERS: Weitz likes the idea of demystifying the unknown.
WEITZ: I mean, the idea of silent space is kind of scary and claustrophobic to me. I like the idea of bringing something human to what I assume is a very inhospitable place.
DETROW: Last week, they held their first ever listening party for the album. They did it at a planetarium in Maryland.

SIMON: One of my favorite parts is we recorded the door opening, which kind of always sounds like Frankenstein coming to life. (Imitating mechanical thumping) Like, it's like this very intense bassy bit. And then it's like...
(SOUNDBITE OF KYLE SIMON AND BRIAN WEITZ'S "THE SIRENS PT. 1")
SIMON: Life, you know? Like, the moon coming in there.
WEITZ: So there are these moments where things threaten to fall apart.
(SOUNDBITE OF KYLE SIMON AND BRIAN WEITZ'S "THE SIRENS PT. 1")
WEITZ: And then I can hear when all of a sudden, like, I just...
(SOUNDBITE OF KYLE SIMON AND BRIAN WEITZ'S "THE SIRENS PT. 1")

WEITZ: ...I get it back together into, like, a harmonious moment. I've learned how to, like, recognize a kindred spirit. I recognized Kyle as one a long time ago. And once you're in those relationships, it's good to just trust that it's going to take you somewhere worthwhile.
DETROW: So as you look out at tonight's full moon, imagine how much it might sound like this one.
(SOUNDBITE OF KYLE SIMON AND BRIAN WEITZ'S "THE SIRENS PT. 1")
